s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling and drainage of serosanguinous fluid from the left labia with signs of sepsis and subcutaneous gas
salient_findings: Progressive swelling of the left labia
Rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid
key_facts: Six-day history of progressive swelling of the left labia
Rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid two days before admission
Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg despite intravenous fluid resuscitation
Pelvic CT imaging showed ulceration of the left labia with air in the subcutaneous fat
Inflammatory fat stranding along the left lateral abdominal wall
LRINEC score 3 with potential to rise to 7

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive swelling, serosanguinous fluid drainage, and subcutaneous gas on CT imaging, along with elevated white blood cell count and LRINEC score

shortlist.label: Fournier gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to necrotizing fasciitis, with a focus on genital and perineal involvement

shortlist.label: Gas gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of subcutaneous gas on CT imaging and signs of sepsis, which are consistent with gas gangrene

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count, hypotension, and signs of sepsis, which are consistent with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome

shortlist.label: Clostridial myonecrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of subcutaneous gas and signs of sepsis, which are consistent with clostridial myonecrosis

raw.rationale: The presence of ulceration, air in the subcutaneous fat, and inflammatory fat stranding on pelvic CT imaging, along with a high white blood cell count and a calculated LRINEC score of 3 with potential to rise, are highly suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis, a severe infection that requires prompt surgical intervention.

rejected.label: Fournier gangrene
rejected.why: While Fournier gangrene is a type of necrotizing fasciitis, it specifically refers to necrotizing fasciitis of the genitalia, and the case description does not exclusively limit the infection to the genitalia, as it involves the lower abdominal wall as well.

rejected.label: Gas gangrene
rejected.why: Gas gangrene typically involves muscle infection with gas production, which is not the primary focus of the case description, where the infection seems to be more superficial, involving the subcutaneous fat and fascia.

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: While this condition can present with severe infection and shock, the case description does not provide specific evidence of streptococcal infection or the characteristic desquamation seen in toxic shock syndrome.

rejected.label: Clostridial myonecrosis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by infection of the muscle with Clostridium species, which is not indicated in the case description, where the focus is on the fascia and subcutaneous tissue rather than the muscle itself.
